## Why

I chose a single, worn **broom** as the sculptural subject. A broom is universally recognized as a tool of humble, practical, daily labor and cleaning, perfectly encapsulating Leo XIII’s definition of Christian Democracy as "beneficent charitable action toward the people" and "organized...charity-driven action on behalf of the poor." It rejects abstraction or complex religious symbols in favor of a concrete object that signifies active, hands-on care and the dignity of labor, rooted in spiritual motivation rather than political ideology or systemic upheaval, distinguishing it sharply from Socialism.

## Text-to-image prompt

I have analyzed the papal text and selected the **broom** as the optimal sculptural symbol to represent *Graves De Communi Re*. This single, mundane object powerfully encapsulates the encyclical’s definition of "Christian Democracy" as humble, practical, non-political charitable service to the poor.

In generating the image, I have adhered strictly to the visual constraints: the object is presented on a checkerboard background to signify transparency for ease of use in design. The centering is precise, the lighting is dramatic with strong contrasts, and the material rendering achieves the requested high-end 3D quality.
